name: Plain Bread Pudding, Baked
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: about a pint of stale bread
ingredients.originalText: about a pint of stale bread

ingredients.name: piece of butter the size of a small egg
ingredients.originalText: a piece of butter the size of a small egg

ingredients.name: one-quarter of a teaspoonful of soda
ingredients.originalText: one-quarter of a teaspoonful of soda

instructions.text: Break up about a pint of stale bread after cutting off the crust, pour over it a quart of boiling milk
Add to this a piece of butter the size of a small egg
Cover the dish tight and let it stand until cool
With a spoon mash it until fine, adding a teaspoonful of cinnamon and one of nutmeg grated, half a cupful of sugar and one-quarter of a teaspoonful of soda dissolved in a little hot water
Beat up four eggs very light and add last
Turn all into a well-buttered pudding-dish and bake three-quarters of an hour
Serve it warm with hard sauce

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Break up about a pint of stale bread after cutting off the crust, pour over it a quart of boiling milk
2. Add to this a piece of butter the size of a small egg
3. Cover the dish tight and let it stand until cool
4. With a spoon mash it until fine, adding a teaspoonful of cinnamon and one of nutmeg grated, half a cupful of sugar and one-quarter of a teaspoonful of soda dissolved in a little hot water
5. Beat up four eggs very light and add last
6. Turn all into a well-buttered pudding-dish and bake three-quarters of an hour
7. Serve it warm with hard sauce
